title: The Periodic Table
seo_title: Year 8 Science: Periodic Table Worksheets (Groups, Periods, Alkali Metals, Halogens)
standard_text: The varying physical and chemical properties of different elements; the principles underpinning the Mendeleev Periodic Table; the Periodic Table: periods and groups; metals and non-metals; how patterns in reactions can be predicted with reference to the Periodic Table; the properties of metals and non-metals.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on the periodic table: groups and periods, Mendeleev, metals and non-metals, alkali metals, halogens and noble gases. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Elements in a group have similar properties.
key_sub: Group 1 gets more reactive going down; group 7 gets less reactive.
body_html:
How to think about it

The periodic table puts elements with similar properties in the same group.

  • Groups are columns, periods are rows. Metals are on the left and in the middle; non-metals are on the right.
  • Group 1 (alkali metals) get more reactive going down. Group 7 (halogens) get less reactive going down.
  • Group 0 (noble gases) are very unreactive.
Example

Potassium or lithium: more reactive?

Lower in group 1

Answer: potassium

Example

Chlorine or iodine: more reactive?

Higher in group 7

Answer: chlorine

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up groups (columns) and periods (rows).
  • Thinking reactivity increases down group 7.
  • Thinking noble gases react easily.

faq.q: What is the difference between a group and a period?
faq.a: A group is a column of elements with similar properties. A period is a row.

faq.q: How do group 1 metals react with water?
faq.a: They fizz and make a metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas. Lithium reacts gently, sodium faster and potassium bursts into a lilac flame.

faq.q: What is a displacement reaction of halogens?
faq.a: A more reactive halogen takes the place of a less reactive one in a compound, for example chlorine displaces bromine from potassium bromide.
